newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain, China haggle over Chinese troops for HK.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China haggle over Chinese troops for HK.

text.p: Britain called on China on Monday to slash the number of troops that Beijing wants to despatch to Hong Kong as an advance party before the territory's handover this year and to reconsider the timing.
The haggling over troops at the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) talks on handover arrangements was the latest in many disagreements in the run-up to the sovereignty change.
Britain hands Hong Kong, its last major colony, back to China at midnight on June 30.
Alan Paul, the British representative at the diplomatic talks, revealed the split at the start of the latest round of talks, covering issues of defence and public order.
"The main issue, I suppose, is that we pointed out to the Chinese side that their proposals for the numbers of advance personnel are too high and timing of their arrival is too early.
"So we put forward a proposal of our own which we regard as reasonable, one which we hope they will consider positively and give us a positive reply at today's meeting," Paul told reporters.

China wants to send an advance party of its People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops who will form the garrison in Hong Kong after Britain withdraws and the territory becomes an autonomous region of China.
Neither side has revealed the size of the PLA contingent China wants to send in before the actual handover.
China has said its garrison might be as large as Britain's was at its peak a decade ago, around 10,000 personnel.
The elite PLA unit has been deployed over the border in the Chinese zone of Shenzhen in recent months, undergoing rigorous military and educational training for the unprecedented mission.
